decisions.reason: Conferencing is peripheral to the firm's network-centric direction and faces strong competition, but the firm has invested in the service and launched it only recently, so it will persist and attribute weak uptake to ramp-up.

The metro data centre network is a capital-intensive infrastructure investment, central to the firm's announced data centre and financial-hub strategy, and is publicly showcased with an adoption success.
Optical spectrum connectivity has its own dedicated page, signalling strong public commitment and sunk fibre investment closely aligned with the firm's core high-bandwidth strategy.
The number ordering portal is a low-cost, recently built digital tool that supports the voice business, so the investment already made and its role in the voice offering justify keeping it.

Carrier pre-selection is a declining legacy telephony service with limited strategic centrality, but existing customers and regulatory context, together with its recent launch, make management inclined to keep it a while longer.
The direct voice network connection rides on established voice infrastructure that the firm has already invested in and fits its enterprise voice portfolio, so it is kept.
